import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

# Training data: y = 2x + 1
x = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype=float)

programs.question: Q5
programs.code:
import tensorflow as tf

# Mean absolute error as a custom loss function
def custom_loss(y_true, y_pred):
    return tf.reduce_mean(tf.abs(y_true - y_pred))

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, input_shape=(1,))
])
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss=custom_loss)

x = tf.constant([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]])
y = tf.constant([[2.0], [4.0], [6.0]])
model.fit(x, y, epochs=5, verbose=0)
print("Training completed with custom loss.")
programs.implementation: Defines mean absolute error and passes it to model.compile().
programs.expected_result: Expected result: training completes and prints the confirmation.

import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

x = np.array([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]])
y = np.array([[2.0], [4.0], [6.0]])

model = tf.keras.Sequential([

programs.question: Q11
programs.code:
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

x = np.arange(1, 11, dtype="float32")
y = 2 * x

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, input_shape=(1,))
])
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")

early_stop = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
    monitor="loss", patience=5, restore_best_weights=True
)
checkpoint = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
    "best_model.keras", monitor="loss", save_best_only=True
)

model.fit(x, y, epochs=100, callbacks=[early_stop, checkpoint], verbose=0)
print("Training finished. Best model saved.")
programs.implementation: Uses EarlyStopping to stop when loss stops improving and ModelCheckpoint to save the best model.
programs.expected_result: Expected result: training finishes and best_model.keras is saved.

import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(64, activation="relu", input_shape=(10,)),

])

              metrics=["accuracy"])

programs.expected_result: Expected result: training completes. Dropout can reduce overfitting, but does not guarantee better results.

programs.question: Q13
programs.code:
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

# Two inputs
input_a = tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,), name="first_input")
input_b = tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,), name="second_input")

combined = tf.keras.layers.Concatenate()([input_a, input_b])
hidden = tf.keras.layers.Dense(8, activation="relu")(combined)

# Two outputs
output_sum = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, name="sum_output")(hidden)
output_product = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, name="product_output")(hidden)

model = tf.keras.Model(
    inputs=[input_a, input_b],
    outputs=[output_sum, output_product]
)
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")

a = np.array([[1.], [2.], [3.], [4.]], dtype="float32")
b = np.array([[2.], [3.], [4.], [5.]], dtype="float32")
sum_y = a + b
product_y = a * b

model.fit([a, b], [sum_y, product_y], epochs=10, verbose=0)
print("Multiple-input, multiple-output training completed.")
programs.implementation: Uses the Functional API to connect two inputs to two output layers.
programs.expected_result: Expected result: training completes without errors.

programs.question: Q14
programs.code:
# Install first: pip install tensorflow keras-tuner
import tensorflow as tf
import keras_tuner as kt
import numpy as np

x = np.random.rand(200, 4).astype("float32")
y = (x[:, 0] + x[:, 1] > 1).astype("float32")

def build_model(hp):
    model = tf.keras.Sequential()
    model.add(tf.keras.layers.Input(shape=(4,)))
    units = hp.Choice("units", values=[8, 16, 32])
    model.add(tf.keras.layers.Dense(units, activation="relu"))
    model.add(tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid"))
    model.compile(
        optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
            learning_rate=hp.Choice("learning_rate", values=[0.01, 0.001])
        ),
        loss="binary_crossentropy",
        metrics=["accuracy"]
    )
    return model

tuner = kt.RandomSearch(
    build_model, objective="val_accuracy", max_trials=3,
    directory="tuning_results", project_name="basic_tuning"
)
tuner.search(x, y, epochs=5, validation_split=0.2, verbose=0)

print("Best settings:", tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(1)[0].values)
programs.implementation: Uses Keras Tuner RandomSearch to test different neuron counts and learning rates.
programs.expected_result: Expected result: the best hyperparameter settings are printed. Install keras-tuner before running.

programs.question: Q15
programs.code:
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.random.rand(300, 4).astype("float32")
y = (x[:, 0] + x[:, 1] > 1).astype("float32")

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(16, activation="relu", input_shape=(4,)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid")
])
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="binary_crossentropy",
              metrics=["accuracy"])

history = model.fit(
    x, y, epochs=20, validation_split=0.2, verbose=0
)

# Plot loss curves
plt.plot(history.history["loss"], label="Training loss")
plt.plot(history.history["val_loss"], label="Validation loss")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("Loss")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Training and Validation Loss")
plt.show()

# Plot accuracy curves
plt.plot(history.history["accuracy"], label="Training accuracy")
plt.plot(history.history["val_accuracy"], label="Validation accuracy")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("Accuracy")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Training and Validation Accuracy")
plt.show()

print("If training improves while validation worsens, overfitting may be occurring.")
programs.implementation: Plots training and validation loss and accuracy to compare model performance.
programs.expected_result: Expected result: two graphs appear. A widening gap between training and validation curves can indicate overfitting.
